findings.finding: 7/8 sampled rows re-fetch to the recorded work (title+first author+year); SRC-057 is PARTIAL only because the row's year 2019 is the Annals print year while the arXiv record is 2017. No locator error found in the sample.

The `year` column mixes preprint-posting and journal years (SRC-057 2019 vs 2017; SRC-081 2025 vs 2024). A mechanical year comparison would report two false mismatches; the column needs a convention note or a separate preprint_year.

5/8 declared quote letters are grounded token-for-token in the fetched abstract, 1 is a metadata record consistent with the fetch, 2 have no abstract in the primary API. No fabricated quotation detected in the sample; the check is abstract-level, not page-level.

Input drift: the audit csv was rebuilt by astra-lead-literature between the sampling freeze (0b72b419) and the first fetch; the harness aborted fail-closed, the pin moved to 315c1914, and the same 8 source_ids were re-verified. G-LIT evidence should cite the csv sha256 with each spot check.

falsifier: A re-fetch of any of the 8 pinned locators that contradicts its ledger row turns the corresponding MATCH into a hard failure and this accept verdict into revise; a page-level check that shows a quote is not in the cited source likewise falsifies the quote-grounding finding.
scope_note: Abstract/metadata-level spot check of 8 of the 55 audit rows not covered by spots #1-#2; it is not a full-ledger review and does not promote any theorem or gate. This is the third independent re-fetch spot check offered as G-LIT evidence.
